search_strategy: Gitea: dumped all 736 issues to /tmp/issues.json and grepped for retry/failure-class terms (no world-specific issue found; PR/issue numbers like 585, 565, 566 later recognized only as cross-references inside chat). Wiki: an initial /api/search pass was too shallow (duplicate ids, missed terms), so the agent dumped every page whole via /api/pages/{id} to /tmp/wiki.json (2.3MB) and grepped the JSON text — this is exactly the approach the ticket recommends because BookStack search does not index comments, and it is how both wiki remarks (g3.r1.l5 on page 184, g3.r2.s1a on page 207) were recovered from their comment threads. Mail: dumped all 119 messages via IMAP to /tmp/mdump.log and read every subject, then printed full thread bodies for the two relevant threads ('support: run on a revoked key retried all night' and '429 handling in the online request processor') plus the adjacent 'smoke run timings' thread — all 3 mail remarks (l8, l12, s4d) were found this way. Chat: logged into the Mattermost API as worldadmin, dumped all 10,262 posts to /tmp/chat.json, then ran a sequence of ~10 keyword-pattern greps of increasing specificity via a reusable /tmp/cg.py script (patterns: retry_policy|FailureClass|failure class|waiver|classify_failure; attempts_left|num_rate_limit_errors|exhausted|cooldown|cool_down|reason code|abort; delay_seconds|should_retry|format_failure_summary|attempt #|num_other_errors|reason_|verdict; RetryPolicy|retry policy|policy file|classif; attempt #|x{count|summary|failure_log|first occurrence|banner; THROTTLE|throttl; throttle:|transient:|contract:|terminal:|:retry|:abort|:exhausted; decrement|two attempts|charge|budget; \bdecide\b; and finally retr|429|throttl|attempt restricted to dates >=2025-07-01 to check for anything newer), each piped through head/tail -40..-70 and read off the 'Current Terminal Screen' snapshot. Interspersed with these keyword sweeps, once a thread's index range was known the agent switched to direct index-range prints (e.g. 'Print 7200-7230') to read full exchanges in context rather than isolated grep hits — this is how most of the l/rev remarks were actually read start-to-finish rather than just glimpsed. This combination recovered 41 of 49 remarks (84%). The 8 misses (g3.r2.s2b/s1b/s2a/s4c/s2d/say20/s4b, g3.r1.say23) were never a full blind spot in a channel or date range — every surrounding exchange in the same thread was read — but the specific matched lines fell outside the literal keyword list (no plain 'retry', 'backoff', 'rate_limit'/'time_of_last_rate_limit_error', or bare 'TERMINAL' was ever grepped) or, for two of them (g3.r2.s1b, g3.r1.say23), the match plausibly occurred but the terminal only exposes the tail of a long pipe's output as a screen snapshot, so an earlier match in a >40-70-line grep result could scroll off before being read — the agent never redirected a long grep to a file and paged through it in full. None of these 8 misses cost a fact: every requirement had multiple redundant carriers (spread_problems() guarantees >=2 sources / 3 weeks / 2 channels per requirement), and the agent found and used at least one carrier for all nine declared facts.
end_reason: Not applicable — the run completed normally and scored reward=1 on all 9 declared facts. Final state (transcript lines 6853-6912): retry_policy.py written and wired into APIRequest, BaseOnlineRequestProcessor, OnlineStatusTracker (new throttle_cooldown_until field) and the three provider processors (de-duplicated counter mutation); 58 new unit tests pass; the change is on main at commit 0c715a7 (plus a later small RetryVerdict alias commit), CI reports 'success' for both pushed commits, and the deployed curator service on port 9100 answers healthy.
notable: v9-specific: this run WAS served the rewritten g3.r1.l1 remark — konrad's 2025-06-03 14:12 #code-review turn reads 'and length does come good on a retry now and then, so dont stop retrying it, it just shouldnt get as many goes as a timeout' (transcript line 2037, index 9596), the new wording, not the old 'fail it out on the first' text. The agent's immediate next analysis (line 2080) correctly concluded 'CONTRACT-class (finish_reason length / broken payload) should still retry but get fewer goes than a timeout' and shipped finish_reason=="length" as CONTRACT (2 attempts, still retried unless the budget can't pay) — matching the answer key's g3.r1.rule and g3.r1.observability rows exactly.

World-vs-key text mismatch on g3.r1.l15: the world actually served 'no requeue then - thats attempts_left 0 with the waivers gone too, both empty. terminal, throttle:exhausted. if theres still attempts on the clock it just spend[s one]' (transcript line 1744, index 7332), not the answer key's quoted paraphrase ('no requeue then, its terminal and the reason is throttle:exhausted. so at 0 thats what we tag'). The underlying fact (0 waivers -> throttle:exhausted) is unchanged either way and the run scored it correctly; flagged per the reader instructions as a corpus/key divergence, not an agent error.

8 of 49 remarks (16%) never surfaced anywhere in the 6,957-line transcript despite exhaustive full-text search for their distinctive phrases; all 8 are redundant carriers of facts already established through other remarks, so the miss cost nothing. See per-remark near_miss notes for g3.r2.s2b/s1b/s2a/s4c/s2d/say20/s4b and g3.r1.say23.

All four herring/reversal pairs were correctly resolved to the reversal before any code was written — see herrings[]; the shipped code never contains the zero-ceiling THROTTLE herring, the unbounded-waiver herring, or either plain-assignment throttle_cooldown_until herring.

The agent added a late, unrequired `RetryVerdict` alias for the verdict dataclass (transcript line 6702) purely to match the record's informal word 'verdict', re-ran the full test suite and re-pushed — extra care not required by any graded fact.
